Bank of England Governor Warns of Populist Threat to Central Bank Independence

Bank of England Governor Andrew Bailey has stated that the rise of populist politicians poses a significant challenge to the independence of central banks. He emphasized the need for central bankers to clearly explain their decisions to the public. Bailey warned that failure to do so risks central bankers being perceived as an "unrepresentative elite," which could undermine public trust and the effectiveness of monetary policy. The comments come amid a broader discussion about the role and perception of independent financial institutions in democratic societies.
